key_insight: EgoForge learns goal-conditioned egocentric world models that jointly simulate rapid camera motion, hand–object interactions, and long-horizon task evolution by inferring latent human intent—enabling realistic, goal-directed egocentric video prediction and simulation.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap in egocentric video generation by modeling fast viewpoint changes, frequent hand–object dynamics, and latent goal-driven procedure evolution without relying on dense supervision like camera trajectories.
method: Goal-conditioned latent intent module that infers and propagates high-level task goals to guide future scene dynamics.
Egocentric dynamics model that explicitly represents camera motion, hands, and object interactions to produce temporally coherent, view-consistent predictions.
Generative renderer/decoder that synthesizes realistic egocentric frames over long horizons, trained with reconstruction and consistency objectives (weak or sparse supervision).
impact: Provides a practical world-simulation backbone for embodied AI, AR/VR, and robot learning—improving long-horizon planning, data augmentation, and realistic training environments from first-person video.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: latent intent inference → egocentric dynamics module → generative renderer (show data flow and conditioning on goal).
Before/after sequence: short input clip vs. long-horizon simulated frames illustrating consistent camera motion and hand–object interactions.
Latent space visualization: trajectories of inferred goals/intent guiding different simulated outcomes (color-coded paths).
Comparison chart: metrics for temporal coherence and goal completion between EgoForge and prior methods (bar or line plot).
paper_authors: Yifan Shen, Jiateng Liu, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu, Bingxuan Li
